Netherlands postcode four digits followed two letters, officially space digits two letters, although often omitted electronic data. naxp accepts forms (treats version space canonical version): ’ve used raw string, r"(...)", naxps use backslashes (like regexes) normal string every backslash doubled. !! syntax means preceding item makes difference encoding whether ’s present, include decoding encoded value back text. naxp maps every postcode fits pattern integer 1 6 760 000, gaps. Let’s take test drive: Note 1012 AB 1012AB mapped encoded value. invalid text, including 1012-AB, mapped 02. can go direction, .e. decode encoded value back text: promised, decoding gives form space, .e. 1012 AB. Note first line need original naxp already included vector’s attributes. Encoded values negative greater maximum raise error: convenience, can check whether text valid naxp convert canonical form without encoding using following functions: can obtain properties naxp:
code: NL_postcode_x <- naxp_parse(r"(\9\9\9\9 \s!! \A\A)") NL_postcode_x #> <naxp> \9\9\9\9 \s!! \A\A #> Maximum encoded value: 6760000 postcodes_as_text <- c("1012 AB", "1012AB", "1012-AB", "not a postcode") postcodes <- naxp_encode(postcodes_as_text, NL_postcode_x) postcodes #> <naxp_encoded[4]> \9\9\9\9 \s!! \A\A #> [1] 1012 AB       1012 AB       <invalid (0)> <invalid (0)> as.integer(postcodes) #> [1] 684114 684114      0      0 naxp_decode(postcodes) # No need for the naxp (NL_postcode_x) #> [1] "1012 AB" "1012 AB" NA        NA naxp_decode(684114L, NL_postcode_x) # Decoding raw numbers requires a naxp #> [1] "1012 AB" naxp_decode(0L, NL_postcode_x) # 0 means invalid -- it decodes to NA #> [1] NA naxp_decode(6760001L, NL_postcode_x) #> Error in `naxp_decode()`: #> ! x[1] is 6760001, above the naxp's maximum encoded value of 6760000. naxp_accepts(postcodes_as_text, NL_postcode_x) #> [1]  TRUE  TRUE FALSE FALSE naxp_canonical_form(postcodes_as_text, NL_postcode_x) #> [1] "1012 AB" "1012 AB" NA        NA writeLines(naxp_pattern(NL_postcode_x)) # Text pattern used to define the naxp #> \9\9\9\9 \s!! \A\A naxp_max_encoded_value(NL_postcode_x) # Maximum encoded value #> [1] 6760000 naxp_max_length(NL_postcode_x) # Maximum decoded text length #> [1] 7

title: Encoded ASCII Expressions
text: Get started
code: library(naxp)  # Assume we have some UK postcodes postcodes_as_text <- c(   "CR2 6XH",   "DN55 1PT",   "M1 1AE",   "EC1A1BB", # The mandated space is sometimes omitted   "not a postcode")  # UK postcodes are complicated so let's grab the standard naxp postcode_naxp <- naxp_standard("uk-postcode") postcode_naxp #> <naxp> \A\A?\9\X? \s!! \9\A\A | GIR \s!! 0AA #> Maximum encoded value: 1755842401  # Encode the text postcodes postcodes <- naxp_encode(postcodes_as_text, postcode_naxp)  # The encoded result looks like text ... postcodes #> <naxp_encoded[5]> \A\A?\9\X? \s!! \9\A\A | GIR \s!! 0AA #> [1] CR2 6XH       DN55 1PT      M1 1AE        EC1A 1BB      <invalid (0)>  # ... but the underlying values are numerical, # with 0 (not NA!) representing invalid text. as.integer(postcodes) #> [1] 180591302 238906246 743107201 277958384         0  # We can recover the canonical text form at any time. # 0 (invalid text) decodes to NA. naxp_decode(postcodes) #> [1] "CR2 6XH"  "DN55 1PT" "M1 1AE"   "EC1A 1BB" NA

code: cat(naxp_emit(r"(\9\9\9\9 \s!! \A\A)", "javascript", prefix = "nl_postcode")) #> /** The naxp this code was generated from. */ #> const nl_postcodePattern = '\\9\\9\\9\\9 \\s!! \\A\\A'; #>  #> /** The largest encoded value this naxp produces, which is also how many it has. */ #> const nl_postcodeMaxEncodedValue = 6_760_000; #>  #> /** The length of the longest string this naxp can decode a value to. */ #> const nl_postcodeMaxLength = 7; #>  #> /** Whether this naxp accepts a string, or the ASCII text in a Uint8Array. A byte outside ASCII is never accepted. #>  * @param {string | Uint8Array} text #>  * @returns {boolean} #>  */ #> function nl_postcodeAccepts(text) { #> 	const bytes = typeof text !== 'string'; #> 	let state = 0; #>  #> 	for (let i = 0; i < text.length; i++) { #> 		const c = bytes ? text[i] : text.charCodeAt(i); #>  #> 		state = nl_postcodeAcceptStep(state, c); #>  #> 		if (state < 0) { return false; } #> 	} #>  #> 	return nl_postcodeIsAccepting(state); #> } #>  #> /** The encoded value of a string, or of the ASCII text in a Uint8Array, from 1 to the largest encoded value, or zero where it is invalid. #>  * @param {string | Uint8Array} text #>  * @returns {number} #>  */ #> function nl_postcodeEncode(text) { #> 	const canonical = nl_postcodeCanonicalise(text); #>  #> 	return canonical === null ? 0 : nl_postcodeRank(canonical); #> } #>  #> /** The string a value stands for, which is in canonical form. #>  * @param {number} value #>  * @returns {string} #>  * @throws {RangeError} The value is not one this naxp produces. #>  */ #> function nl_postcodeDecode(value) { #> 	if (value < 1 || value > nl_postcodeMaxEncodedValue) { #> 		throw new RangeError('This naxp encodes the values 1 to 6760000.'); #> 	} #>  #> 	return String.fromCharCode.apply(null, nl_postcodeDecodeCore(value)); #> } #>  #> /** The string a value stands for, as ASCII bytes. #>  * @param {number} value #>  * @returns {Uint8Array} #>  * @throws {RangeError} The value is not one this naxp produces. #>  */ #> function nl_postcodeDecodeToBytes(value) { #> 	if (value < 1 || value > nl_postcodeMaxEncodedValue) { #> 		throw new RangeError('This naxp encodes the values 1 to 6760000.'); #> 	} #>  #> 	return Uint8Array.from(nl_postcodeDecodeCore(value)); #> } #>  #> /** The string a value stands for, which is in canonical form, or null where the value is not one this naxp produces. #>  * @param {number} value #>  * @returns {string | null} #>  */ #> function nl_postcodeTryDecode(value) { #> 	if (value < 1 || value > nl_postcodeMaxEncodedValue) { return null; } #>  #> 	return String.fromCharCode.apply(null, nl_postcodeDecodeCore(value)); #> } #>  #> /** The canonical form of a string, or of the ASCII text in a Uint8Array, or null where it is invalid. #>  * @param {string | Uint8Array} text #>  * @returns {string | null} #>  */ #> function nl_postcodeGetCanonicalForm(text) { #> 	const canonical = nl_postcodeCanonicalise(text); #>  #> 	return canonical === null ? null : String.fromCharCode.apply(null, canonical); #> } #>  #> /** The code points of the canonical form of a string, or of the ASCII text in a Uint8Array, or null where it is invalid. */ #> function nl_postcodeCanonicalise(text) { #> 	const bytes = typeof text !== 'string'; #> 	const canonical = []; #> 	let state = 0; #>  #> 	for (let i = 0; i < text.length; i++) { #> 		const c = bytes ? text[i] : text.charCodeAt(i); #>  #> 		state = nl_postcodeCanonicalStep(state, c, canonical); #>  #> 		if (state < 0) { return null; } #> 	} #>  #> 	return nl_postcodeFinishCanonical(state, canonical) ? canonical : null; #> } #>  #> /** The rank of a canonical string, as code points, within the canonical language, or zero where it is not in it. */ #> function nl_postcodeRank(codes) { #> 	const acc = { total: 0 }; #> 	let state = 0; #>  #> 	for (let i = 0; i < codes.length; i++) { #> 		state = nl_postcodeEncodeStep(state, codes[i], acc); #>  #> 		if (state < 0) { return 0; } #> 	} #>  #> 	return nl_postcodeIsCanonicalAccepting(state) ? acc.total + 1 : 0; #> } #>  #> /** The code points of an encoded value already checked against the largest one. */ #> function nl_postcodeDecodeCore(value) { #> 	const codes = []; #> 	const box = { remaining: value }; #> 	let state = 0;
